tools.name: aml_exchange_deposit_check
tools.title: Exchange deposit check
tools.description: Checks one address: is it a deposit address of a centralized exchange (Binance, Bitget, Bybit, Coinbase, Gate, KuCoin, MEXC, OKX, ...), of which exchange, and into which hot wallet was it swept, how many times, by which path and when. It reads the SWEPT links of the address and its cex_role (deposit, hot_wallet, cold_wallet or withdrawal) on the graph, and its behaviour as counts (how many addresses paid it, how many it paid, how many of each are exchange wallets, the DEX pools it swapped on, the spenders it approved), anchored on the address: six reads in one batch, billed as any read. Use it when a trail reaches an address that may be an exchange wallet, when the user asks where money entered an exchange, or when someone says an address is an exchange deposit: a claim is never proof, the answer of this tool is. A deposit address is one customer's: everything it sends goes to the wallets of one exchange (a sweep into a hot wallet), few outside addresses ever pay it, it never swaps on a DEX, and it is no token, pool, router or smart account. The graph judges that, never you: the verdict is is_deposit, cex_role and swept. Give behaviour and does_not_fit_deposit as the facts behind it, and never set a threshold of your own for payers, volume or sweeps. With no deposit mark an address is not shown to be a deposit, whoever says it is one; with found false it has no activity on the network, and the claim is unproven there. An answer with inferred: true is the exchange model's prediction, not a listed source: report the address as inferred by the model, with its version (inferred_model), never as a confirmed exchange address. Money that reaches an exchange deposit with a SWEPT link entered that exchange there: the trail ends at the deposit, and never walks on past a hot wallet. Take an exchange's wallets from meta_exchange_lookup, never from a guess or a graph search by name.

network.description: Network to query: robinhood, the one public network. CIA does not pick a default network, so always pass it. meta_network_capabilities (no arguments) lists the live networks.

address.description: The address to check: 0x plus 40 hex characters, any case. An exchange name is not an address: call meta_exchange_lookup first.
